headline: Renesas has introduced a new gallium nitride power transistor, cooled from both sides, aimed at the power systems of AI data centers.
score_reason: Vendor product launch with company-stated gains and 2027 volume production; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: More compact power parts could help data center builders handle megawatt-scale racks, which touches operators and server makers, but the benefits are Renesas's own figures and mass production is a year away.
summary: Bisinfotech reports, relaying a Renesas Electronics announcement, that the company has released a 650-volt gallium nitride (GaN) transistor, a power chip, in a package cooled from both top and bottom, for AI racks whose power needs are rising from about 120 kilowatts toward megawatts. Renesas says the package cuts board area by 57% against a larger top-cooled design; samples are with select customers and mass production is due in mid-2027.
